implementation_statement: Group POL-02 Access Control Policy (P06) applies to the OFP. OFP access procedures (role request runbooks for the ERP, WMS, portal, and FFE) are maintained by the platform team.

Workforce accounts come from SYS-G1 identity governance driven by HR events and federate to the ERP, WMS, portal, and FFE. FFE accounts are approved by the integration center managers and certified quarterly. Gap: DC-8 and DC-9 (acquired 2025) still use 22 shared handheld logins in the WMS.
evidence: Identity governance export; FFE certification 2026-Q2; WMS user list

implementation_statement: Provisioning, disabling, and certification campaigns are automated in SYS-G1 identity governance for every federated OFP application.
Accounts unused for 60 days are disabled automatically; the FFE tenant disables after 35 days.

Role-based access is enforced in the ERP (about 340 roles), the WMS, the portal, and the FFE. Gap: about 2,300 CUI-marked documents sit as sales order attachments in the commercial ERP and about 900 in the commercial collaboration tenant, outside the FFE. Purge and an attachment block on DoD orders are due 2026-11-15.
evidence: ERP role catalog; CUI discovery scan 2026-06-22

implementation_statement: The FFE accepts CUI only through the prime secure file exchange and its own upload service. Gap: no technical control stops staff from attaching CUI to commercial ERP orders or emailing it from the commercial tenant. Data loss prevention rules for CUI markings are due 2026-12-15.
evidence: FFE data flow diagram; DLP design

implementation_statement: Segregation of duties rules in the ERP separate supplier master changes, purchase order approval, and payment release; FFE administrators cannot approve their own access.
evidence: ERP segregation of duties ruleset; conflict report

implementation_statement: Least privilege is applied through role design; ERP administrators reduced to 14 in 2026. FFE technicians hold job-scoped roles.
Security functions (identity, logging, key management) are restricted to named group administrators through PAM.
Privileged access to OFP components is granted just in time through PAM with approval and session recording.
Privileged functions in the ERP, WMS, FFE, and cloud consoles are logged and forwarded to the SIEM.
Accounts lock after 10 failed attempts; risk-based sign-in blocking is enabled.
A use notice appears at SSO sign-in and on FFE workstations, including the CUI notice text.
Managed workstations lock after 10 minutes idle; FFE lab workstations after 5 minutes.
ERP and portal sessions end after 30 minutes idle; FFE sessions after 15 minutes.
Remote access to OFP administration uses the group zero-trust access service with MFA and device checks; FFE remote access is limited to managed devices in the government-community tenant.

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Remote sessions use TLS 1.2 or higher with FIPS-validated modules for the FFE path.
evidence: Access service configuration; module certificates list

implementation_statement: DC and integration center wireless uses enterprise authentication; handheld SSIDs are separate from corporate SSIDs; no wireless in the integration center labs.
Mobile devices are enrolled in device management; CUI is blocked on mobile devices.

External system use is governed by POL-05. Gap: the commercial collaboration tenant was used for CUI exchange with two primes (about 900 files). Migration to the government-community tenant is due 2026-11-30.
Reseller portal catalog content is reviewed before publication; no FCI or CUI is published.
Annual security awareness training and quarterly phishing exercises for all workforce; 97% completion in 2026.
Role-based CUI training is in place for FFE users. Gap: receiving authenticity and anti-counterfeit training is delivered at 4 of 9 DCs only.
The group logging standard defines events for identity, administration, data access, and configuration change.
Log records carry user, source, time, object, and outcome; FFE file access logs include document identifiers.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The SOC reviews correlated alerts 24x7; weekly review of FFE file access reports by the integration center managers.
evidence: SOC case records; FFE weekly review sign-off

implementation_statement: SIEM correlation integrates identity, EDR, cloud, ERP, and FFE logs.
Systems synchronize to provider time services and the group time source.
Logs are stored in a write-once archive account with restricted access.
Logs are retained 1 year online and 3 years archived, which covers the 90-day preservation duty after a DFARS report.
Log generation is enabled on OFP components and verified monthly against the data source list.

Group internal audit assessed common controls and OFP samples in 2026 (P07). Gap: the 2025 SP 800-171 Basic Assessment covered the FFE servers only, not the integration center lab networks or the CUI found in the ERP.
One POA&M (P07) tracks OFP weaknesses with owners and dates; CMMC POA&M eligibility is flagged per item.
Continuous monitoring through the SIEM, monthly vulnerability reports, and quarterly control health dashboards.
Baselines exist for cloud images, WMS servers, handhelds, and FFE lab workstations.
Changes follow the group change process with a change advisory board; FFE changes need integration center manager approval.
Guardrail policies enforce configuration settings in both landing zones; FFE workstations follow a hardened benchmark.
Unneeded services are disabled in images; FFE workstations run an application allow list.

Cloud assets are inventoried automatically. Gaps: the IC-2 lab inventory missed 31 test devices, and about 1,900 SKUs in the ERP item master have no manufacturer of record, which weakens Section 889 screening.
Users cannot install software on managed endpoints; FFE workstations block it entirely.
The OFP contingency plan covers the ERP, WMS, portal, and FFE, with recovery order from the BIA (P05).
regulatory_driver: None (business requirement: P05 BIA; 3PL client service commitments, P09 A1.2 and A1.3)

implementation_statement: WMS and ERP integration restores are tested quarterly. Gap: no test has covered ransomware reaching the WMS replica, and the FFE restore was last tested in 2025.
regulatory_driver: None (business requirement: P05 BIA; 3PL client service commitments, P09 A1.2 and A1.3)

implementation_statement: Immutable backups in a separate provider B account for the WMS, integration layer, and portal exports; FFE snapshots every 4 hours in the government-community region.
Backup integrity is checked by quarterly restores and automated hash checks.
Recovery runbooks rebuild WMS and FFE components from infrastructure code and restore data from the vault.
regulatory_driver: None (business requirement: P05 BIA; 3PL client service commitments, P09 A1.2 and A1.3)

implementation_statement: Users are uniquely identified through SYS-G1 for all federated OFP applications. Gap: 22 shared handheld logins at DC-8 and DC-9.
Phishing-resistant MFA for all privileged access.
MFA for all workforce network access to the OFP, including FFE workstation sign-in.
Identifiers are assigned from HR records and never reused.
Authenticator management follows the group standard; service account secrets are rotated every 90 days in the secrets vault.
Passwords of at least 14 characters, checked against breached-password lists.
About 1,900 3PL client users sign in to the WMS client console with passwords only. MFA through the customer identity service is planned for 2026-12-31.
regulatory_driver: None (3PL client contract commitments; P09 CC6.1)

implementation_statement: Technical playbooks are tested quarterly. Gap: no cross-division exercise has tested a product-integrity incident with DoD, customer, and SEC notices.
The group SOC handles incidents with one severity scale and playbooks, including P08.
Incidents are tracked in the case system with discovery dates recorded for each notice clock.
Incidents are reported through POL-03. Gap: only 2 people hold DoD-approved medium assurance certificates for DIBNet, both at Federal Solutions headquarters.
The group incident response plan and the P08 runbook are approved.
Maintenance of OFP infrastructure is scheduled through change records; FFE lab equipment maintenance is logged.
Maintenance tools for the FFE labs are approved and stored in the lab cage.
Vendor maintenance of OFP components uses PAM-brokered sessions with MFA and recording.
Maintenance personnel in the integration centers are escorted unless authorized for CUI.
CUI media access is limited to the CUI user roster.
CUI media is stored in locked cabinets inside the lab cages.
Media from the FFE is sanitized under NIST SP 800-88 by Lifecycle Services with certificates.
Removable storage is blocked on managed endpoints except issued encrypted drives; FFE workstations block all removable storage.
DC badge access lists are managed by Logistics; integration center cage lists are approved by the integration center managers.
Badge readers, cameras, and guards at all DCs; cage access at IC-1 and IC-2. Gap: at IC-2 visitor escorts during the night dock shift were not recorded in 2 of 6 sampled weeks.
Cameras with 90-day retention at docks and integration center cages; guard patrols.
Visitor logs are electronic and kept 1 year.
Remote work rules apply; CUI is not handled at alternate work sites.
This SSP covers the OFP. Gap: the FFE section did not describe the integration center lab networks until this version; the CMMC scope description is being finalized.
Rules of behavior (POL-05) are acknowledged at hire and annually.
The group information security program plan (POL-01) covers all divisions and the OFP.
The group risk management strategy sets acceptance authority by risk level (P01).
The group C-SCRM strategy (NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1) covers suppliers for all divisions.
Background screening before access, plus CUI roster checks for FFE users.
HR termination events disable SYS-G1 accounts within 4 hours.
Information types are categorized in section 6 of this SSP; CUI is Moderate confidentiality at minimum.
regulatory_driver: N42-R03 (252.204-7012(b)); 32 CFR 2002.14(g) (CUI at no less than moderate confidentiality)

implementation_statement: Group and division risk assessments under SP 800-30 (P01).
Monthly authenticated scans of cloud and server assets. Gap: IC-2 lab network devices were not in scan scope until 2026-07.
Risk responses are tracked in the registers and the POA&M.
Critical components and product lines are identified for federal orders.
Contracts include security requirements; supplier terms include FAR 52.204-25 and DFARS 252.246-7008 flowdown for federal-eligible suppliers.
External services are reviewed annually. Gap: the commercial ERP vendor holds CUI attachments but has no FedRAMP Moderate equivalency evidence (DFARS 252.204-7012(b)(2)(ii)(D)).
Unsupported components are tracked; handhelds at DC-8 and DC-9 are scheduled for replacement in 2027.
Landing-zone hubs and firewalls protect OFP boundaries. Gap: the IC-2 lab network has a route to the DC-6 corporate VLAN for a label printer.

control_name: Deny by Default, Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Deny-by-default rules apply at landing-zone hubs and the FFE boundary.
Data in transit uses TLS 1.2 or higher.
Cryptographic protection in transit for all OFP paths; FIPS-validated modules on the FFE paths.
Network sessions terminate after inactivity.
Keys are managed in provider key management with customer-managed keys for the FFE.
FIPS-validated cryptography protects CUI in the FFE.
Collaboration devices in integration centers have no remote activation.
Data at rest is encrypted in all OFP stores.
Encryption at rest uses provider modules validated under FIPS 140 for the FFE.
Critical patches within 14 days for servers and endpoints; WMS patches through change windows.
EDR on all managed endpoints and servers, including FFE workstations.
24x7 monitoring of OFP components through the SIEM.
Inbound and outbound traffic at hubs and the FFE boundary is monitored for unusual patterns.
Threat advisories, including OEM firmware advisories, are reviewed daily.
Firmware and software integrity checks run on devices staged in the integration centers. Extending hash or signature checks to receiving at all DCs is planned for 2027-03-31.
Group C-SCRM policy and procedures (POL-01 section 4).
Group C-SCRM plan covers suppliers for all divisions and is reviewed annually.

Supply chain controls include authorized-source rules for federal orders. Gap: the Section 889 block does not cover Lifecycle refurbished stock; DFARS 252.246-7008 flowdown to 180 brokers is incomplete.
Provenance is recorded for federal integration jobs (serials and source). Gap: serial-level provenance is not captured at receiving for 5 of 9 DCs.
Acquisition strategies prefer authorized sources. Gap: buyers can still select brokers for commercial stock without risk review.
Authorized distributors are assessed annually. Gap: 61 of 180 brokers have no assessment.
Notification agreements with authorized suppliers require notice of compromise.
Receiving inspection with OEM serial validation at 4 of 9 DCs; physical tamper checks at all DCs. Gap: 5 DCs lack serial validation.
Anti-counterfeit policy exists. Gap: detection relies on receiving checks that are incomplete (SR-10).
regulatory_driver: DFARS 252.246-7008(b)(1)-(2) (prime subcontracts); DFARS 252.246-7008(b)(3)(ii) (prime subcontracts); DFARS 252.246-7008(c) (prime subcontracts)

implementation_statement: Anti-counterfeit training for buyers and integration technicians. Gap: receiving staff at 5 DCs not trained.

control_name: Configuration Control for Component Service and Repair
implementation_statement: Configuration control for components serviced in the integration centers.
Component disposal through Lifecycle Services with sanitization certificates.
